facts.text: The package provides a 2-D simulator for mobile robots in ROS 2; robots move through a cmd_vel topic and may publish a laser scan.
The Simulation node advertises a service to spawn robots in, wrapped by the spawn executable.
The spawn node is run in the same namespace as the robot_description topic, and that namespace is used to publish the robot topics.
Spawning a robot twice resets only its pose; other parameters are changed by removing and re-spawning the robot.
The cmd_vel topic is subscribed by the simulator for each robot according to its namespace, and by default the scan topic is used unless a Gazebo plugin names another topic.
Spawn.srv defines SHAPE_SQUARE=0, SHAPE_CIRCLE=1 and SHAPE_RECTANGLE=2, followed by the request members and an empty response after the separator.
SimulatorNode registers the absolute /simulator/spawn service whose callback calls addRobot, and the /simulator/add_anchor service.
The SimulatorNode class declares two ROS service members, spawn_srv and anchor_srv, and no other service member.
SimulatorNode::addRobot appends a trailing slash to the requested namespace and, for an existing robot, calls resetTo with the requested pose instead of creating a new robot.
Robot::resetTo assigns the requested pose, writes it to initial_pose when that transform has a child frame, and clears odom.pose.pose and odom.twist.twist.
Robot::loadModel assigns odom_pub from create_publisher<nav_msgs::msg::Odometry>(robot_namespace + "odom", 10).
Robot::loadModel creates a geometry_msgs/Twist subscription on <robot_namespace>cmd_vel; the callback copies only linear.x, linear.y and angular.z into odom.twist.twist.
parseLaser defaults to 100 samples and the relative scan topic.

Without a Gazebo ray plugin and with force_scanner true, loadModel sets angle_max=49*M_PI/50, angle_min=-angle_max, range_min=0.1, range_max=5, resizes the ranges array to the sample count and creates the LaserScan publisher.
SimulatorNode computes dt=1/declare_parameter("rate", 20) and drives refresh from a wall timer.
SimulatorNode::refresh calls robot.move(dt) only for connected robots, then recomputes the laser scans and publishes each connected robot.
Robot::initFromURDF waits 500 ms and subscribes to <robot_namespace>robot_description with transient-local QoS; the callback calls loadModel with the received description text.
Robot::move integrates the pose from the stored odom.twist.twist velocities, each passed through withNoise, on every call.
Robot::publish assigns odom.header.stamp and transform.header.stamp from its now argument and then publishes odom.
Pose2D::writeTo(geometry_msgs::msg::Pose) assigns pose.position.x, pose.position.y, pose.orientation.w and pose.orientation.z.
Robot::move constructs a Pose2D from odom.pose.pose, calls updateFrom and then writeTo(odom.pose.pose).
withNoise returns val * (1 + std * unit_noise(random_engine)), where unit_noise is a static std::normal_distribution<double>(0, 1).
SimulatorNode::addRobot reads spec.robot_namespace.back() without checking for an empty namespace.
With the display enabled, a double click in the OpenCV window calls removeRobotAt, which removes the robots at that pixel.
The README says a robot is unspawned by double-clicking it, which cannot be done with display false.
The TurtleBot3 example spawns its robot in the namespace given by the name argument, default turtlebot1, and starts slider_publisher with cmd_vel.yaml in that namespace.
The multi-robot example starts slider_publisher with cmd_vel_multi.yaml and spawns robots in the namespaces r2d2, r2d3 and r2d4.
Robot.__init__, when cmd_type is not None, reads declare_parameter('pub_cmd', True).value and, when that value is true, creates a Twist publisher on the relative topic 'cmd_vel' with queue size 5.
Robot.publish publishes self.cmd_vel on self.cmd_vel_pub when self.cmd_vel_pub is not None.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned responses; no physics step, pacing, collision response, laser cast or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free canned transport: it answers the declared /simulator/spawn, /robot1/cmd_vel, /robot1/odom and /robot1/scan messages and runs no map_simulator, OpenCV, occupancy-grid, collision, laser or wall-clock code

the odom and scan values are placeholders. An /robot1/odom subscription returns a short burst: its first sample is the stored twist (the confirmation discards it) and later samples snap to the last cmd_vel. A non-zero cmd_vel steps the stored pose by a placeholder dt of 0.1 so the command is observable, and that projection is not stored as the odom twist; two reads with no new command agree. A zero command stores a still pose and a zero twist. This is not Robot::move, withNoise or an occupancy-grid ray cast

the real simulator creates the odom and scan publishers only after a robot_description message arrives (src/robot.cpp:113-126, 170-214); the fake starts with a placeholder /robot1 robot and does not model that handshake

the real default scan is 100 samples with angle_max=49*M_PI/50 and range 0.1..5 unless a Gazebo ray plugin overrides it (src/robot.cpp:131-132, 194-211); the fake returns 100 placeholder samples and does not parse a URDF or a scan-topic remapping
the package exposes only one robot namespace; a multi-robot or differently namespaced deployment needs per-robot absolute endpoints and is NOT COVERED

/robot1 is this package's deployment choice: no shipped launch spawns it (the examples use /turtlebot1 or /r2d2, /r2d3 and /r2d4 and also start slider_publisher, a competing cmd_vel publisher); until a robot is spawned in /robot1 and its robot_description arrives, /robot1/odom and /robot1/scan do not exist, the resource read fails NOT_READY and every command, the first spawn included, waits the 2 s read timeout before completing (reviewer probe on the fake)

the simulator keeps integrating the last cmd_vel command on every refresh until another command or a duplicate spawn arrives (src/robot.cpp:219-226, 282-293); an empty robot_namespace reaches std::string::back() in addRobot (src/simulator.cpp:55-57)

the sensed stop covers /robot1 only, and only inside its confirmation window. slider_publisher (example/turtlebot3/turtlebot3_world_launch.py:8-36 and example/multirobot/multi_launch.py:21-46) and kinematics.py when pub_cmd is true (src/kinematics.py:101-103, 121-122) are other cmd_vel publishers; if one keeps publishing, the confirmation fails closed. A duplicate spawn calls resetTo (src/simulator.cpp:53-65, include/map_simulator/robot.h:135-143) and is not a stop. Removing a robot is a GUI double click (src/simulator.cpp:28-36). The client bounds are not source facts; a live deployment sets them in simulation_deployment['estop_confirmation']

the package does not expose /simulator/add_anchor, /tf, /joint_states, /ranges, the map_server lifecycle or any unspawn, pause, reset or step service. kinematics.py is disclosed above and is not a command of this package
the fake is a canned stand-in, not a recording of captured ROS traffic and not the upstream simulator

confirmation.description: Simulated only: /robot1/odom position x and y and orientation z and w stay within the operator span, and linear.x, linear.y and angular.z stay within the operator absolute bound, for three consecutive fresh stamped samples inside the confirmation bound. A zero Twist on /robot1/cmd_vel proves nothing; another cmd_vel publisher can move /robot1 again; nothing is claimed beyond that window or for any other robot.
predicate: max - min of odom.pose.pose.position.x over the window <= rest_x
max - min of odom.pose.pose.position.y over the window <= rest_y
max - min of odom.pose.pose.orientation.z over the window <= rest_qz
max - min of odom.pose.pose.orientation.w over the window <= rest_qw
